attachments.origin_landmark: inner surface of a lower rib, near its angle
attachments.insertion_landmark: inner surface of the second or third rib below

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Present mainly in the lower thorax; they span more than one intercostal space, which is what distinguishes them from the innermost intercostals.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: High-frequency linear probe in longitudinal (parasagittal) orientation over the lower posterior/posterolateral intercostal spaces (this muscle is most consistently present at the lower thoracic wall, ribs 10-12, and variably higher), following the rib's curvature. This is the standard approach for an intercostal nerve block at these levels.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Subcostales lie in the same deep muscular plane as the innermost intercostals and transversus thoracis, spanning from the internal surface of one rib across one or more intervening ribs to a rib below; the parietal pleura is directly deep to it, and the intercostal neurovascular bundle runs in the plane immediately superficial to it.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Two or more adjacent hyperechoic rib shadows with the hypoechoic muscle layers spanning between them; the pleura is seen as a bright sliding line immediately deep to this muscle, moving with respiration.
structures_at_risk: pleura and underlying lung (pneumothorax) -- the standard named hazard of any needle advanced into the lower intercostal spaces, and a particular risk here given this muscle's direct relationship to the pleura
intercostal vessels running with the nerve just superficial to this muscle
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: No motor-point/neural-arborization mapping for this muscle's own belly was found in the literature searched -- unsurprising, since it is often absent or rudimentary and is not individually distinguished from the innermost intercostals on clinical ultrasound. What is well documented is the ultrasound-guided intercostal nerve block at these lower thoracic levels, whose target plane runs directly superficial to this muscle -- included here because it is the real clinical 'injection approach' relevant to this muscle's neurovascular plane, not a claim of an intramuscular BoNT target.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Kannan A, Srinivasan S (2026) 'Image-Guided Interventions for Intercostal Neuralgia: What the Radiologist Needs to Know', J Med Imaging Radiat Oncol, doi:10.1111/1754-9485.70151 -- review of ultrasound- and CT-guided intercostal nerve block/ablation technique
